title: Sūrat al-Wāqiʿah 15–24 — The Inevitable: the paradisal reception of the foremost

translation.sourceText: Arabic Qur'anic text from earliest-attested Hijazi-script manuscripts (Tübingen Ma VI 165 for Sūrat al-Anbiyāʾ; Codex Parisino-petropolitanus for Sūrat al-Qamar and Sūrat al-Wāqiʿah); modern Cairo Hafs reference vocalization

verdicts.reasoning: *Wildān muḫalladūn* rendered 'youths of unaging endurance' preserves the classical-tafsīr ambiguity between 'eternally-youthful' and 'immortalized' readings (rejects Asad's 'perpetual freshness' and Pickthall's 'never altering in age' as leaning 'eternally-youthful'). The Luxenberg 'fruits everlasting' disavowal is verbatim and named-cite (Stewart 2008; Neuwirth 2003; Saleh 2008 — three of the most-respected specialist rejections). The Raëlian-canon cloning-immortality disavowal is verbatim. Cross-corpus chain to Greek symposium-cup-bearer tradition / Pesaḥ-reclining / messianic-banquet documented as parallel-banquet-tradition. The surface 'youths of unaging endurance' would read as a defensible Arberry-register rendering to a scholarly reader.

citations: al-Ṭabarī Jāmiʿ al-Bayān ad loc. (both 'they do not run out' and 'they do not become drunk' readings)
Sura 37:46-47 parallel formulation (lā fīhā ġawl wa-lā hum ʿanhā yunzafūn)
verdicts.reasoning: *Lā yuṣaddaʿūna wa-lā yunzafūn* 'neither pained with headache nor brought to depletion' preserves the classical-tafsīr ambiguity of *yunzafūn* between 'they do not run out [of wine]' and 'they do not become drunk/depleted.' 'Brought to depletion' covers both. *Yuṣaddaʿūn* 'they are afflicted with headache' (from *ṣudāʿ*) literal-philological.

*Fākiha mimmā yataḫayyarūn* 'fruit of their choosing' lexically accurate. *Yataḫayyarūn* Form V 'they choose for themselves' correctly rendered. Cross-corpus to Gen 2:9 / Rev 22:2 noted in commentary as typological-shared paradise-fruit topos.

citations: Sura 52:22; 76:14-15 parallels (laḥm + paradise vocabulary)
verdicts.reasoning: *Laḥm ṭayr* 'flesh of fowl' literal-philological (hapax legomenon in the Qurʾān). *Yaštahūn* 'they desire' Form VIII of š-h-w/y. No lens-leakage.

citations: Jarrar 2002 'Houris' in Encyclopaedia of the Qurʾān Brill (the standard modern philological survey)
Stewart 2008 in Reynolds ed.; Neuwirth 2003 JQS; Saleh 2008 in Reynolds ed. (Luxenberg-rejection)
Tirmidhī Sunan 2562 (the weak ḥadīth source of the '72 virgins' figure — classed ḥasan-gharīb)
wadud 1999 Qur'an and Woman; Barlas 2002 Believing Women (gender-symmetric paradisal-description reading)
verdicts.reasoning: *Ḥūr ʿīn* rendered 'wide-eyed companions' is the most-distinctive lens-discipline rendering in the chapter and is defensible: it preserves the gender-ambiguity of the Arabic plural (the singular *aḥwar* m. / *ḥawrāʾ* f. could describe either gender; Jarrar 2002 EQ). The five-stratum disavowal architecture is exemplary: (1) classical-tafsīr gendered-female reading documented but flagged as 'going beyond what the ayah itself specifies'; (2) Asad/Pickthall/Khalidi gender-ambiguity-preserving readings noted; (3) **Luxenberg 'white grapes' disavowal verbatim with Stewart 2008 / Neuwirth 2003 / Saleh 2008 named**; (4) **'72 virgins' orientalist-stereotype disavowal verbatim with Tirmidhī 2562 ḥasan-gharīb classification noted and 'NOT IN THE QURʾĀN' capitalized**; (5) **Raëlian-canon paradisal-companion-civilization disavowal verbatim**. Wensinck-tested: Tirmidhī 2562 falls in *Kitāb Ṣifat al-Janna* and is correctly classed *ḥasan-gharīb* by Tirmidhī himself. amina wadud 1999 / Barlas 2002 feminist-Quranic-scholarship correctly cited as supporting gender-symmetric reading. The surface English ('wide-eyed companions') would pass scholarly inspection as a register-neutral rendering.

verdicts.reasoning: *Ka-amṯāli l-luʾluʾi l-maknūn* 'like the likeness of sheltered pearls' lexically accurate. *Maknūn* 'sheltered / kept hidden / treasured-up' (passive participle of k-n-n) preserved. The Matt 13:45-46 cross-corpus correctly typologized as 'precious-treasure-hidden' shared topos, NOT 'Quranic pearl = Christological-kingdom pearl' (verbatim disavowal in commentary).

verdicts.reasoning: *Jazāʾan bi-mā kānū yaʿmalūn* 'a recompense for what they used to do' preserves the *kānū yaʿmalūn* habitual-imperfect-past correctly in 'used to do.' Cross-corpus to Jewish-Christian-Quranic *erga / maʿasîm / aʿmāl* works-tradition typologized as shared-tradition, NOT collapsed ('not interchangeable' verbatim). Closes the 56:15-24 paradisal-reception passage cleanly.

glossaryReview.reasoning: claim_type=direct defensible: the five reading-strata each have direct documentation (classical tafsīr explicit; Asad/Pickthall/Khalidi published renderings explicit; Luxenberg 2000 published explicit; the '72 virgins' Tirmidhī 2562 source explicit; the Raëlian canon explicit). The four verbatim disavowals (Luxenberg / 72-virgins-orientalist-stereotype / Raëlian-canon / classical-tafsīr-overreach) are unambiguous and named-cite. The 'wide-eyed companions' rendering is well-grounded in the grammatical-gender-ambiguity of the Arabic. The exemplary disavowal-architecture entry of the entire corpus to date.

glossaryReview.reasoning: claim_type=direct defensible: the five-passage paradisal-reception cluster (56:15-26; 76:5-21; 83:25-28; 37:41-49; 52:17-24) is documented in Neuwirth 2014. The Wansbrough late-canonization-thesis is correctly preserved as historical-critical apparatus and explicitly not endorsed, against the Sadeghi-Goudarzi 2010 / Hilali 2017 manuscript-evidence nuancing.

notes.official: The 56:15-24 passage opens the paradisal-reception of the *as-sābiqūn* / *al-muqarrabūn* 'the foremost / the brought-near' class — the highest of three eschatological classes introduced at Sura 56:7-14 (with *aṣḥāb al-yamīn* 'companions of the right' and *aṣḥāb al-shimāl* 'companions of the left'). The tripartite division has cross-corpus parallels in the Matt 25:31-46 sheep-and-goats separation and the rabbinic three-classes-judgment tradition (m. Roš ha-Šānāh 1:1-2; b. Roš ha-Šānāh 16b-17a); typological-shared Near-Eastern eschatological-classification structure, not 'these traditions are the same.' *Mawḍūnah* (passive participle of w-ḍ-n) is variously glossed in classical tafsīr (Ṭabarī cites Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid: 'woven of gold', 'inlaid with jewels', 'closely-wrought'); the 'closely-wrought' rendering preserves the literal w-ḍ-n metalworking-sense without committing to specific inlay-material (Arberry-style, against Asad's 'gold-encrusted' and Pickthall's 'inwrought with gold and precious stones').

i18n.en: reclining upon them, facing one another.

notes.official: The *muttakiʾīn ... mutaqābilīn* 'reclining ... facing one another' encodes the Greco-Roman-Eastern symposium / banquet-couch posture; cross-corpus to the *triclinium* (D. E. Smith 2003 *From Symposium to Eucharist*), the Jewish *Pesaḥ*-reclining-as-free-person trope (m. Pesaḥim 10:1), the messianic-banquet parables (Matt 22:1-14; Luke 14:15-24), and the Isa 25:6 Yahweh-banquet on Mount Zion. Documented as Late-Antique Near-Eastern shared-paradisal-banquet topos (Neuwirth 2014).

i18n.en: Among them circulate youths of unaging endurance,

notes.official:
The *wildān muḫalladūn* is a major lens-risk site. The Form II passive participle *muḫalladūn* (from ḫ-l-d 'to be eternal') preserves an irreducible classical-tafsīr ambiguity between (a) 'eternally-youthful — their youth never fades' and (b) 'immortalized — they never die'; Ṭabarī, Qurṭubī preserve both readings without firm preference. The 'unaging endurance' rendering preserves both without committing (against Asad's 'youths of perpetual freshness' which leans (a), and Pickthall's 'youths never altering in age' which also leans (a)).

Lens-discipline disavowals (per glossary entry *wildan-mukhalladun-...-luxenberg-disavowed-raelian-disavowed*): (i) Luxenberg 2000's Syro-Aramaic re-reading as 'fruits everlasting' is academically rejected by Stewart 2008, Neuwirth 2003, Saleh 2008 and the WoH-Translation does not adopt it. (ii) The Raëlian-canon reading of *muḫallad* as cloning-derived immortality on the Elohim home planet is acknowledged as a source-of-record reading that this entry does not endorse as the source-text's primary meaning. Cross-corpus to the broader Near-Eastern symposium / cup-bearer tradition (Greek *Symposium*; Pesaḥ-reclining; Matt 22:1-14 messianic-banquet) noted as typological-shared.

i18n.en: with goblets, ewers, and a cup from a flowing spring —

notes.official: The drinking-vessel triad has high loanword-density that Neuwirth 2014 reads as evidence of Quranic situatedness in the multilingual Late-Antique Near East: *kūb* < Greek *kúpē* / Aramaic *kūbā*; *ibrīq* < Persian *ābrīz*; *kaʾs* cognate with Hebrew *kōs* (Ps 23:5; Ps 16:5; Isa 51:17; Jer 25:15). The cross-corpus drinking-vessel-of-the-righteous tradition (the Pesaḥ four cups; the eucharistic cup; the messianic-banquet cup at Matt 26:27-29) is typological-shared paradisal-banquet topos.

i18n.en: by which they are neither pained with headache nor brought to depletion;

notes.official: The paradisal-wine-without-effects clause distinguishes paradisal wine from earthly wine (which the Qur'an condemns at Sura 2:219; 5:90-91). *Yuṣaddaʿūn* 'they are afflicted with headache' is stable in classical tafsīr; *yunzafūn* preserves a classical-tafsīr ambiguity between (a) 'they do not run out [of wine]' and (b) 'they do not become drunk / depleted' — Ṭabarī preserves both readings. 'Brought to depletion' preserves both. Parallel at Sura 37:46-47.

*Fākiha* 'fruit' is a recurrent paradisal vocabulary item (cluster-parallel at Sura 37:42; 38:51; 43:73; 44:55; 52:22; 55:11; 55:52; 55:68; 56:32; 77:42; 80:31). Part of the Meccan-eschatological-paradisal-cluster compositional grouping (Neuwirth 2014).

i18n.en: and the flesh of fowl, of what they desire.

notes.official: *Laḥm ṭayr* 'fowl-flesh' as paradisal-banquet element; parallel within the Meccan-eschatological-paradisal-cluster at Sura 52:22 and Sura 76:14-15.

The *ḥūr ʿīn* is the most-discussed lens-risk site in this passage. The phrase compounds *ḥūr* (plural; from ḥ-w-r 'eye-white intensely-white, iris intensely-dark') and *ʿīn* (plural; 'wide-eyed') — both pre-Islamic Arabian beauty-descriptors. The 'wide-eyed companions' rendering preserves the gender-ambiguity of the Arabic (the plural *ḥūr* is grammatically feminine but the singular *aḥwar* m. / *ḥawrāʾ* f. could describe either gender; Jarrar 2002 'Houris' in EQ Brill).

Five reading-strata are documented and four are explicitly disavowed (per glossary entry *hur-al-ayn-...-luxenberg-disavowed-orientalist-stereotype-disavowed-cross-corpus*): (i) the classical Sunni tafsīr (Ṭabarī, Zamakhsharī, Qurṭubī, Ibn Kathīr) gendered-female reading is documented but goes beyond what the ayah itself specifies; (ii) Asad / Pickthall / Khalidi gender-ambiguity-preserving readings noted; (iii) **Luxenberg 2000's Syro-Aramaic re-reading as 'white grapes' is academically rejected** (Stewart 2008; Neuwirth 2003; Saleh 2008) and not adopted; (iv) **the popular Western '72 virgins' orientalist stereotype is NOT in the Qur'an** — the figure derives from a single weak ḥadīth in Tirmidhī 2562 (classed *ḥasan-gharīb*, not in the *Ṣaḥīḥān*), the Qur'an specifies no number, and the WoH-Translation explicitly disavows the stereotype; (v) the Raëlian-canon paradisal-companion-civilization layering at *Extra-Terrestrials Took Me To Their Planet* is acknowledged-without-endorsement.

i18n.en: like the likeness of sheltered pearls —

notes.official: *Maknūn* (passive participle of k-n-n 'to conceal, to treasure'): 'kept hidden / treasured-up / sheltered'. The simile compares the *ḥūr ʿīn* of v. 22 to the *luʾluʾ maknūn* sheltered-pearls. Parallel formulations at Sura 52:24 and 76:19 (in the *wildān muḫalladūn* context). Cross-corpus to Matt 13:45-46 (the parable of the pearl of great price) — typological-shared 'precious-treasure-hidden' metaphor, not 'the Quranic pearl IS the Christological-kingdom pearl.'

i18n.en: a recompense for what they used to do.

notes.official: The standard Quranic recompense-by-deeds formula closing the paradisal-reception description. Cross-corpus to Matt 16:27 ('he shall reward every man according to his works'); Rev 22:12 ('I come quickly, and my reward is with me, to give to every man according as his work shall be'); m. Avot 2:16 ('It is not your duty to complete the work, but neither are you free to desist from it ... and the Master of your work is faithful, who will pay you the reward of your labor'). The Quranic *jazāʾ* / *aʿmāl* 'recompense / works' sits within the Jewish-Christian-Quranic *erga* / *maʿasîm* / *aʿmāl* 'works' tradition — typological-shared, not 'these traditions are interchangeable.' The *kānū yaʿmalūn* habitual-imperfect-past is preserved in the 'used to do' rendering. This ayah closes the paradisal-reception passage and the Meccan-eschatological-paradisal-cluster grouping.
